name: Koh Phangan
tagline: Full Moon beach, quiet coves and jungle hills
summary: Known for the Full Moon Party at Haad Rin, but most of the island is quiet: yoga and sunsets on the west coast, remote coves in the north-east. Rent a scooter or use taxis and pick one coast as a base.
seasonNote: The Gulf islands are wettest from October to December, the opposite of Phuket and Krabi. Prices triple around each full moon.
arrival: No airport. Fly to Koh Samui and take a 30-minute ferry, or fly to Surat Thani and use a bus and ferry ticket (about 4 hours).
gettingAround: Shared songthaew taxis charge fixed, high prices; most visitors rent scooters, but the hill roads are steep and accidents are common.
cashTip: Bring cash for taxis, boats and markets; ATMs cluster in Thong Sala and Haad Rin.
foodTip: Eat at the Thong Sala night market, and look for southern curries and fresh seafood barbecues on the beach.
buyTip: The Saturday walking street in Thong Sala has crafts and clothes.
baseArea: Srithanu or Haad Yao for calm and sunsets; Haad Rin for the party; Thong Nai Pan for a remote beach

connections.note: Ferry to Samui or the mainland, then a flight.

items.name: Haad Rin and the Full Moon Party
items.summary: A crescent of white sand that hosts the monthly all-night beach party for up to 30,000 people.
items.expect: On party nights: loud, crowded and messy, with a 200 baht entry fee. On other days it is a pleasant, quiet beach.
items.tip: Check the date before booking; wear shoes on the sand and leave valuables in the hotel safe.

items.summary: A boat day among 42 limestone islands with kayaking, snorkelling and a steep viewpoint.
items.expect: A full day with an early start; the viewpoint climb is 500 metres of ropes and steps.
items.tip: Choose a speedboat for less travel time; the park closes in November.
